newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium outlines conditions for working with Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Belgium outlines conditions for working with Zaire.

text.p: Belgium said on Saturday it was ready to cooperate with Zaire's new government if it opened its doors to other political groups, held democratic elections and dealt humanely with the country's refugee problem.
Foreign Minister Erik Derycke said it was too soon to say, however, whether Belgium recognised the regime of rebel leader Laurent Kabila, who said on Saturday he was taking over as head of state.
"We have set out the basis on which we could work with a government," he told a news conference. "Now it is up to Zaire's government, even while it is an interim one, to react."
Derycke also said Belgians in Zaire appeared to be out of danger in the wake of president Mobutu Sese Seko's departure and the entry of Kabila's forces into the capital Kinshasa.
"The greatest danger is past for our compatriots, although we must remain cautious," he said.
Derycke said Belgium wanted Zaire to hold elections, but could accept a reasonable delay to ensure they were "true" elections.
"There are two types of elections in Africa -- those that are forced and those that are well prepared," he said.
